message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 atm) water is still above its triple‑point pressure (≈ 0.006 atm), so it can exist as solid, liquid, or vapor.  
From the water phase diagram the melting/freezing line drops roughly linearly from 0 °C at 1 atm to –2.2 °C at 10 kPa.  
Thus the freezing point of water at 10 kPa is **about –2.2 °C** (≈ –2 °C).
